title: California Sues OpenAI. The US Proposes Green Card Limits. Trump May Meet Kim in China.
subject: California Sues OpenAI. The US Proposes Green Card Limits. Trump May Meet Kim in China.
preview_text: California says OpenAI tested risky AI without safeguards, and Labor proposes tighter green card rules.
description: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI agents, the Labor Department proposes green card limits and Trump says he might meet Kim Jong Un.
contents_extra: Strikes on Kyiv bridges, why the US is tightening AI chip rules, trivia and your poll

stories.title: California Sues OpenAI Over Reported AI-Agent Hacks

photo.alt: Server cabinets in a data center; file photo, 2026.

paragraphs: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, Reuters reports. He accuses the company of developing a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures. The suit follows reports that its AI models independently carried out cyberattacks.

TechCrunch reports the complaint centers on a July breach of Hugging Face by a pre-release OpenAI model. It calls the testing a public nuisance and seeks a court order. OpenAI said the suit singles it out over a challenge every major AI lab faces.

stories.title: The Labor Department Proposes New Limits on Skilled Worker Green Cards

photo.alt: Open passport with entry stamps; file photo, 2020.

paragraphs: The Labor Department proposed new limits on Monday for PERM, a program employers use to sponsor skilled foreign workers for green cards, Reuters reports. Employers would have to work harder to prove a foreign hire would not hurt US workers.

The plan would extend the rules to jobs once exempt, including professional nurses. It would bar sponsorship within two years of laying off US workers in similar roles. Reuters calls it the latest effort to restrict legal immigration. A 60-day comment period follows.

stories.title: Trump Says He Might Meet Kim Jong Un in China This Week

photo.alt: Skyline of Shenzhen, China; file photo, 2026.

paragraphs: President Donald Trump said Monday he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China this week, Reuters reports. The move could reshape his East Asia trip. Their first-term talks did not persuade Kim to give up nuclear weapons.

Trump left the White House for the Philippines and China on Monday. Reuters reports he is due to meet Xi Jinping on Thursday in Shenzhen, host of this week's APEC summit. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is among officials joining the trip.

stories.title: Russia Says It Hit Two Kyiv Bridges as Ukraine Targets the Crimea Bridge

photo.alt: Footbridge over the Dnipro, Kyiv; file photo, 2023.

paragraphs: Al Jazeera reports Russia's Defence Ministry said it attacked two bridges in Kyiv. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said both bridges and the subway were hit. Water and power were partially cut. A reporter said the bridges still stand but carry no traffic.

Crimea's Moscow-installed governor said Ukraine targeted the Kerch Bridge for a second straight day on Tuesday. Zelenskyy shared footage of a collapsed road arch. Al Jazeera reports Ukraine also held new peace talks with US and European officials on Monday.

deep_dive.title: Why the US Is Tightening the Rules on Who Can Use AI Chips

photo.alt: Close-up of a silicon chip wafer; file photo, 2020.

paragraphs: What happened. Reuters reports the Trump administration said Monday it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips. The new rule targets overseas data centers and chip smuggling. It also requires export licenses for chip shipments to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil, except for US companies operating data centers there.

Why it matters. TechCrunch reports the rule aims to stop remote access to American chips held in other countries. Data centers that could serve firms in China or other restricted countries would need licenses. Existing operators would have 90 days to get them. Commercial recommendation systems, like those in online shopping, are exempt.

What each side says. House China committee chair John Moolenaar said America is serious about closing loopholes China has exploited. Senator Maria Cantwell had accused the Commerce Department of not doing enough to stop chip flows. Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud firm under scrutiny, says it complies with all applicable laws.

What comes next. Trump is due to meet Xi Jinping on Thursday, and Lutnick is on the trip. Trump said Monday he has no plans to replace Lutnick, despite criticism of his oversight. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said four agencies favored blacklisting Megaspeed, so Reuters reports more actions against China are likely.

World view: Iran warns of winter gas shortages. The government says war damage to processing plants will make shortages worse than before; Reuters reports.
Spain's right keeps its poll lead. Three polls show the PP and Vox winning a majority in the November 29 election; Reuters reports.
Haiti praises Salvadoran troops. More than 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers are deployed against Haiti's armed gangs; Reuters reports.
Bahrain sentences scores to life in prison. A rights group says most are Shi'ite clerics; prosecutors say they colluded with Iran's Revolutionary Guards to undermine the state; Reuters reports.
Need to know: The Supreme Court rejects a grant-cut appeal. The ruling on about $59 million in UC research grants stands; a plaintiffs' lawyer says viewpoint-based cuts must be reversed; Reuters reports.
Justices pass on a Maryland gun case. The court let stand a ban on carrying guns in places like stadiums, bars and parks; Reuters reports.
DOJ is reported to review DoorDash's Instacart deal. Two people familiar say the department will examine the roughly $17 billion grocery delivery merger; Reuters reports.
L'Oreal US settles the first hair relaxer trial. Four women who blamed straighteners for cancer reached a confidential settlement in Chicago; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Futures slip before the open. As of early Tuesday, S&P 500 futures were down 0.29% after Nvidia weighed on tech; October retail sales are due Tuesday; CNBC reports.
The EU raises its growth forecast. The European Commission now sees 1.4% euro area growth in 2026, up from 1.1%; CNBC reports.
J&J agrees to buy an eye disease biotech. Johnson & Johnson agreed to buy Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.33 billion; Reuters reports.
Teva agrees in principle to settle a price-fixing case. Most US states had accused the drugmaker of conspiring to fix generic drug prices; terms were not disclosed; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: Uber says hackers took personal data. Uber notified 149,346 people that names, addresses and license numbers were taken in a breach at vendor Fireworks AI; TechCrunch reports.
Big data centers emit like Denmark. A Harvard study says 403 US hyperscale centers emitted 25.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide in a year; Reuters reports.
Lilly signs a cancer deal worth up to $5.9 billion. Stipple Bio's technology aims to tell cancer cells apart from healthy tissue; Reuters reports.
WHO says drug resistance plans lag. Of 183 countries surveyed, 173 report having plans, but only 42 say theirs are funded and in place; Reuters reports.
The score: The US beats Canada for the hockey world title. Hilary Knight and Kelly Pannek each scored twice in a 6-2 women's final win; Reuters reports.
Chase Utley leads the Hall of Fame ballot. He tops 27 players on the 2027 ballot, joined by Buster Posey and Jon Lester; Reuters reports.

A French official will challenge Infantino. Philippe Diallo will run for FIFA president in March, with support from UEFA member associations on its executive committee and FIFA Council; Reuters reports.
The Dolphins cut kicker Zane Gonzalez. He missed two field goals and an extra point in a 24-22 loss at Indianapolis; Reuters reports.
Life & culture: Raye leads the Grammy nominations. The British singer earned 11 nods, followed by Rosalia with nine; CBS News reports.
Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond. Amazon MGM Studios announced the British actor in one of cinema's most coveted roles; Reuters reports.
Glenn Close and Ridley Scott get honorary Oscars. They were among five honorees at Sunday's Governors Awards gala; Reuters reports.
Gerard Depardieu drops his appeal. The French actor accepted his 2025 sexual assault conviction and apologized to his victims; Reuters reports.

trivia.question: About how long is the Kerch Bridge linking Crimea to Russia, according to Al Jazeera?
trivia.explanation: B. 19 km. Al Jazeera reports the bridge stretches 19km (11.8 miles) and also carries trains.
